newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares closer lower as nerves creep in.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares closer lower as nerves creep in.

text.p: Sweden's sharemarket lost its earlier gains in afternoon trading on Wednesday as nerves crept in ahead of Wall Street's opening and with a possible vote of no confidence against Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson.
Even though New York opened firmer, the Stockholm general index failed to regain lost ground and closed 0.24 percent lower at 2207.71 after shares worth 4.0 billion crowns were traded.
"Much will depend for Thursday and Friday on how Ericsson and Astra perform in the U.S. tonight," one broker said.
He said several days of lower closes in Stockholm had added an element of uncertainty into the market.

Drugs major Astra closed 1.5 crowns higher at 311.5 crowns on Wednesday while telecoms giant Ericsson slipped three to 197 crowns. NatWest downgraded its trading recommendation on Ericsson to accumulate from buy which caused a few jitters.
A possible vote of no confidence against Persson for comments he made in China that were seen as praising China's political stability added a hint of uncertainty to the market.
A top performer was retailer Hennes & Mauritz that closed 25 up at 970 crowns. Brokers said this was due better retail sales, lower interest rates and an announced 1998 launch in France.
